messages.content: I experimented briefly wtih imitation yesterday and got 72.8% accuracy on validation (last day) for all decks, that translate in about 600 ELO on leaderbord. I found that conditioning on player ELO gives a 2% accuracy increase out of the box, and it can somewhat extrapolate conditioning up to 2000ELO. Clearly it doesn't get an ELO of 2000, but it get a 2% win rate improvement against my rule based agents panel compared to condiyioning to 1300

messages.content: How consistent is imitation learning in this setting? I get about 79% consistency. With the exact same code, different submissions can end up anywhere from rank 50 to rank 150, and it all comes down to whether the initial few matches are wins.
messages.rawMarkdown: How consistent is imitation learning in this setting? I get about 79% consistency. With the exact same code, different submissions can end up anywhere from rank 50 to rank 150, and it all comes down to whether the initial few matches are wins.

messages.content:
How are you measuring 79% consistency? You mean policy accuracy or how do you measure it?

Also, if you mind sharing. Imitation learning is based of one deck (or set of similar decks), or many different decks and players. This also might be related to higher lower consistency as far as I can see (mixed distributions).
